column1: # DDR gene panel — 25 genes evaluated in the prespecified DDR pathway analysis
# (Methods §2.2; Results; Fig. 1).
# COLUMN DEFINITIONS
#   gene              : HGNC-approved gene symbol
#   in_pritchard_2016 : TRUE if the gene is among the 20 DDR genes profiled in
#                       Pritchard et al. NEJM 2016 (Inherited DNA-Repair Gene
#                       Mutations in Men with Metastatic Prostate Cancer);
#                       FALSE otherwise. Provides traceability to the
#                       prostate-cancer-specific DDR panel that motivated this
#                       study's gene selection.
#   in_broca          : TRUE if the gene is in the University of Washington
#                       BROCA hereditary cancer-risk panel (Walsh et al. 2010;
#                       ongoing updates); FALSE otherwise. BROCA is the
#                       clinical cancer-susceptibility panel used for germline
#                       testing across hereditary cancer syndromes.
#   pathway_core      : DDR pathway membership under Knijnenburg et al. 2018
#                       (Cell Reports) core-pathway taxonomy. Categories:
#                       BER, NER, MMR, FA, HR, NHEJ, DR (Direct Repair),
#                       TLS (Translesion Synthesis), DamageSensor.
#                       "DDR-modulator" = gene not in Knijnenburg's panel but
#                       with literature-supported DDR-regulatory role; the
#                       affected pathway (where specific) is noted in parens.
#                       "NA" = not annotated in Knijnenburg or core pathway
#                       not assigned.
#   pathway_broad     : Knijnenburg's broader multi-pathway annotation
#                       (slash-delimited). Categories: BER, NER, MMR, FA,
#                       HDR (Homology-dependent Recombination), NHEJ, DR, TLS,
#                       NP (Nucleotide pools), Others.
#   source            : Knijnenburg 2018 for genes in the 276-gene annotated set;
#                       explicit secondary citation for the 6 genes not in
#                       Knijnenburg's panel (DDX11, FMN2, MET, MYC, TEX15, TRAIP).
# REFERENCES
#   Pritchard CC et al. "Inherited DNA-Repair Gene Mutations in Men with Metastatic
#     Prostate Cancer." N Engl J Med 2016; 375:443-453.
#     The 20-gene Pritchard panel: ATM, ATR, BARD1, BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, CHEK1,
#     CHEK2, FAM175A, FANCA, GEN1, MLH1, MRE11A, MSH2, MSH6, NBN, PALB2, PMS2,
#     RAD51C, RAD51D.
#   Walsh T et al. "Detection of inherited mutations for breast and ovarian
#     cancer using genomic capture and massively parallel sequencing."
#     BROCA Cancer Risk Panel (University of Washington; ongoing updates):
#     67-gene hereditary cancer susceptibility clinical panel.
#   Knijnenburg TA et al. "Genomic and Molecular Landscape of DNA Damage Repair
#     Deficiency across The Cancer Genome Atlas." Cell Reports 23, 239-254 (2018).
#     Supplementary Table S1 lists 276 DDR genes with pathway annotations.
#   MET literature: Medova M, Aebersold DM, Zimmer Y. "MET inhibition in tumor
#     cells by PHA665752 impairs homologous recombination repair of DNA double
#     strand breaks." Int J Cancer 130, 728-734 (2012). Medova M et al. "The
#     Molecular Crosstalk between the MET Receptor Tyrosine Kinase and the
#     DNA Damage Response." Cancers 6, 1-27 (2014) [review].
#   MYC literature: Luoto KR et al. "Tumor cell kill by c-MYC depletion: role
#     of MYC-regulated genes that control DNA double-strand break repair."
#     Cancer Res 70, 8748-8759 (2010). Giuntini F, Whitfield JR, Masso-Valles D,
#     Soucek L. "The leading role of MYC in DNA damage response." Front Cell
#   FMN2 literature: Belin BJ, Lee T, Mullins RD. "DNA damage induces nuclear
#     actin filament assembly by Formin-2 and Spire-1/2 that promotes efficient
#     DNA repair." eLife 4:e07735 (2015). Originally identified as an ATM/ATR
#     phosphorylation substrate in Matsuoka S et al. "ATM and ATR substrate
#     analysis reveals extensive protein networks responsive to DNA damage."
#   TEX15 literature: Yang F, Eckardt S, Leu NA, McLaughlin KJ, Wang PJ.
#     "Mouse TEX15 is essential for DNA double-strand break repair and
#     chromosomal synapsis during male meiosis." J Cell Biol 180, 673-679 (2008).
#     Schopp T et al. "TEX15 is an essential executor of MIWI2-directed
#     transposon DNA methylation and silencing." Nat Commun 11, 3739 (2020).
#     Both functions are germ-cell-specific; TEX15 inclusion in a somatic-cell
#     DDR panel relies on the assumption that meiotic DSB-repair mechanisms
#     (RAD51 loading) extrapolate to somatic contexts.
#   POLG literature: Park J, Herrmann GK, Mitchell PG, Sherman MB, Yin YW.
#     "Polgamma coordinates DNA synthesis and proofreading to ensure
#     mitochondrial genome integrity." Nat Struct Mol Biol 30, 812-823 (2023).
#     Longley MJ, Nguyen D, Kunkel TA, Copeland WC. "The fidelity of human
#     DNA polymerase gamma with and without exonucleolytic proofreading and
#     the p55 accessory subunit." J Biol Chem 276, 38555-38562 (2001).
#     POLG performs replication-coupled proofreading (3'->5' exonuclease) in
#     mtDNA replication and is annotated by Knijnenburg as the mitochondrial
#     BER polymerase. Both activities are restricted to the mitochondrial
#     compartment, distinct from nuclear DDR pathways.
#   RIF1 literature: Chapman JR, Barral P, Vannier JB, Borel V, Steger M,
#     Tomas-Loba A, Sartori AA, Adams IR, Batista FD, Boulton SJ. "RIF1 is
#     essential for 53BP1-dependent nonhomologous end joining and suppression
#     of DNA double-strand break resection." Mol Cell 49, 858-871 (2013).
#     Escribano-Diaz C, Orthwein A, Fradet-Turcotte A, et al. "A cell
#     cycle-dependent regulatory circuit composed of 53BP1-RIF1 and
#     BRCA1-CtIP controls DNA repair pathway choice." (2013). Gupta R,
#     Somyajit K, Narita T, et al. "DNA Repair Network Analysis Reveals
#     Shieldin as a Key Regulator of NHEJ and PARP Inhibitor Sensitivity."
#     Cell 173, 972-988 (2018). RIF1 is the proximal 53BP1 effector in NHEJ;
#     53BP1-RIF1 antagonizes BRCA1-CtIP-mediated end resection and recruits
#     Shieldin to DSBs.
#   WRN literature: Chan EM, Shibue T, McFarland JM, et al. "WRN helicase is
#     a synthetic lethal target in microsatellite unstable cancers." Nature
#     Picco G, et al. "Prioritization of cancer therapeutic targets using
#     CRISPR-Cas9 screens." Nature 568, 511-516 (2019) [companion paper].
#     WRN is a RecQ DNA helicase; depletion induces DSB accumulation
#     selectively in MSI (MMR-deficient) cancers. WRN resolves D-loops and
#     insertion-deletion loops; has documented roles in HR, NHEJ, and
#     replication-fork stability. WRN deficiency causes Werner syndrome
#     (premature aging, cancer predisposition).
# PANEL COMPOSITION SUMMARY
#   Cross-reference of the 25 panel genes against three external panels:
#     - Pritchard 2016 (PCa-specific DDR mutation panel): 10/25 overlap
#         (ATM, ATR, BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, CHEK2, MSH2, NBN, PALB2, RAD51C)
#     - BROCA (clinical hereditary cancer-risk panel): 13/25 overlap
#         (ATM, ATR, BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, CHEK2, MET, MSH2, MSH3, NBN, PALB2,
#          RAD51C, TP53)
#     - Knijnenburg 2018 (pan-cancer DDR taxonomy): 19/25 in the 276-gene
#       annotated set; 6 are not (DDX11, FMN2, MET, MYC, TEX15, TRAIP) and
#       are annotated from secondary literature where available.
#   Genes supported by secondary primary literature (not in canonical panels,
#   or in Knijnenburg "Others" only):
#     - DDX11 (Pisani et al. 2018) — Warsaw breakage syndrome / FA-like
#     - FMN2  (Belin et al. 2015 eLife) — nuclear actin / DSB repair;
#             ATM/ATR substrate per Matsuoka et al. 2007
#     - MET   (Medova et al. 2012; Ganapathipillai 2008) — HR impairment
#     - MYC   (Luoto et al. 2010; Vafa et al. 2002) — DSB repair gene control
#     - POLG  (Park et al. 2023 Nat Struct Mol Biol; Longley et al. 2001
#             J Biol Chem) — mitochondrial DNA polymerase; replication-coupled
#             proofreading (3'->5' exonuclease) and Knijnenburg-annotated
#             mitochondrial BER. Mitochondrial-compartment-restricted, distinct
#             from nuclear DDR pathways.
#     - RIF1  (Chapman et al. 2013 Mol Cell; Escribano-Diaz et al. 2013;
#             Gupta et al. 2018 Cell) — proximal 53BP1 effector in NHEJ;
#             antagonizes BRCA1-CtIP-mediated end resection; recruits Shieldin
#             to DSBs. Clinically relevant to PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in
#             BRCA1-deficient contexts. Knijnenburg annotates as NHEJ in broad
#             scheme.
#     - TEX15 (Yang et al. 2008 J Cell Biol; Schopp et al. 2020 Nat Commun) —
#             meiotic DSB repair / RAD51 loading; germ-cell-specific function
#             (somatic role is an extrapolation).
#     - TRAIP (Hoffmann et al. 2016 Mol Cell) — FA pathway-adjacent
#     - WRN   (Chan et al. 2019 Nature; Behan et al. 2019 Nature [companion]) —
#             RecQ helicase; depletion induces DSB accumulation; synthetic
#             lethal in MSI (MMR-deficient) cancers; roles in HR, NHEJ, and
#             replication-fork stability. Knijnenburg annotates as BER/HDR
#             in broad scheme.
#   Notes:
#   - DamageSensor (ATM, ATR, CHEK2) in Knijnenburg's core taxonomy corresponds
#     to what is sometimes labeled "checkpoint" or "HR/checkpoint" in other
#     classifications.

column6: Belin et al. 2015 (eLife); FMN2 nucleates nuclear actin filaments in response to DNA damage; depletion increases DSB foci. Originally identified as ATM/ATR substrate in Matsuoka et al. 2007 (Science).

column6: Medova et al. 2012 (Int J Cancer); MET inhibition impairs HR repair of DSBs. Ganapathipillai et al. 2008 (Cancer Res); MET-RAD51 coupling via Abl. Reviewed in Medova et al. 2014 (Cancers).

RIF1
column6: Knijnenburg 2018 (NHEJ in broad scheme). Chapman et al. 2013 (Mol Cell); RIF1 essential for 53BP1-dependent NHEJ and suppression of DSB end resection. Escribano-Diaz et al. 2013; 53BP1-RIF1 vs BRCA1-CtIP cell-cycle circuit controls DSB repair pathway choice. Reviewed in Gupta et al. 2018 (Cell); RIF1 is the proximal 53BP1 effector recruiting Shieldin for NHEJ.

column1: TEX15
column6: Yang et al. 2008 (J Cell Biol); TEX15 essential for meiotic DSB repair and RAD51/DMC1 loading. Schopp et al. 2020 (Nat Commun); TEX15 essential for piRNA-directed transposon silencing. CAVEAT: both functions are germ-cell-specific; somatic DDR role is an extrapolation.

column1: TP53
TP53BP1
TRAIP
column6: Hoffmann et al. 2016 (Mol Cell); FA pathway-adjacent replication-fork ubiquitin ligase

column1: WRN
column6: Knijnenburg 2018. Chan et al. 2019 (Nature); WRN is a RecQ helicase whose depletion induces DSBs and is synthetic lethal in MSI cancers (MMR-deficient cells); WRN resolves D-loops and insertion-deletion loops. Behan et al. 2019 (Nature; companion study); independent CRISPR identification of WRN as MSI cancer dependency. WRN also has documented roles in NHEJ and HR.
